## Ownership and integration

Each encoder exclusively borrows Writer; each decoder borrows Reader. Plain and dictionary codecs also borrow DataType, while BinaryDecoder selects the Arrow byte-array type through its generic parameter and stores nullable. DictionaryDecoder owns an ArrayRef for already loaded values. Constructors store state without general file-bound or schema validation; DictionaryDecoder::new asserts the outer dictionary shape, and PlainDecoder::new unconditionally returns Ok. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/binary.rs:38-47; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/binary.rs:107-151; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/plain.rs:32-42; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/plain.rs:211-224; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/dictionary.rs:26-36; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/dictionary.rs:80-120)

~~~text
V1 writer page adapter
|-- PlainEncoder: primitive bytes / joined Boolean bits / recursive FSL values
|-- BinaryEncoder: payload bytes -> absolute Int64 position table
`-- DictionaryEncoder: PlainEncoder for keys only

V1 reader page adapter
|-- PlainDecoder: range IO -> array reconstruction
|-- BinaryDecoder: PlainDecoder positions -> payload range(s)
`-- DictionaryDecoder: PlainDecoder keys + supplied dictionary values
~~~

The page adapters store the encoder return as PageInfo.position and summed logical rows as length. Dictionary values travel separately through schema dictionary hydration; the reader adapter unwraps both dictionary metadata and loaded values before constructing its decoder. Complete local reader and writer lifecycles are now covered in their supplements; full Dataset/backend lifecycle remains pending. ## Binary layout and null semantics

For N rows, write the sliced payload spans in order, then N+1 absolute Int64 byte positions. Return the position-table start, not the first payload byte. The first position is Writer::tell before payloads; later array offsets are rebased to the current absolute end. The raw Int64 buffer is written without explicit endian conversion or framing. A nonempty list of empty arrays writes one endpoint; an empty input slice asserts. Exactly Utf8, Binary, LargeUtf8 and LargeBinary are supported; views return InvalidInput. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/binary.rs:48-105)

The encoder ignores original validity. Decoder nullable=true marks equal adjacent positions null, so valid empty values become null and null slots retaining nonempty payload cannot be distinguished from valid values. nullable=false returns all values valid, including empty spans. This is a frozen representation rule, not a universal null-preserving binary codec. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/binary.rs:61-86; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/binary.rs:165-232)

Range reads first fetch N+1 Int64 positions through PlainDecoder, subtract the first absolute position and cast offsets to Int32 for small byte arrays. Payload IO is skipped when start>=end; otherwise request that absolute byte range. Array construction is fallible, but negative/nonmonotone offsets and exact response size have no dedicated local checks. The internal endpoint assertion is weaker than the subsequent endpoint access. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/binary.rs:153-233; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/binary.rs:394-415)

## Selection rules and IO cost

| Behavior | BinaryDecoder | PlainDecoder and dictionary key reads |
|---|---|---|
| Empty range beyond logical length | Reject if end exceeds length before empty check | Return empty before bounds/type checks |
| Reversed range with end in bounds | Return empty | Return empty |
| RangeFrom starting beyond length | Return empty reversed range | Return empty reversed range |
| Multiple Ranges | InvalidInput | InvalidInput |
| Empty Indices | Typed empty, no IO | Typed empty, no IO |
| Take planning | Full first-to-last position span; fixed 64KiB byte-distance threshold | Reader block size; Boolean-specific block arithmetic |
| Ordering validation | Sorted-input assumption, no sorting; null index unwraps during sizing | Raw selector values drive planning without sorting or null preflight |

Selection evidence: rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/binary.rs:286-328; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/binary.rs:394-428; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/plain.rs:306-343; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/plain.rs:374-439; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/dictionary.rs:122-174.

Binary takes precompute the sum of selected value lengths, allocate payload and N+1 offsets, read planned chunks with ordered buffered(reader.io_parallelism), then copy a contiguous chunk once or gather each requested value. The position span can be large for two far-apart rows; a contiguous value run can exceed the nominal 64KiB threshold. Output is materialized even when the range-reader payload can share Bytes storage. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/binary.rs:246-390)

Plain takes keep consecutive rows in the same chunk regardless of block_size, and otherwise split by distance from the chunk's first row. Boolean takes split on row/(block_size*8). Both read enclosing ranges, apply Arrow take and retain all decoded chunk arrays before concat. The IO threshold is not a maximum request size; zero/truncated Boolean block sizes and unchecked arithmetic remain assumptions. FixedSizeList<Boolean> range decoding can recurse, while take calls byte_width, which is unavailable for its Boolean child. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/plain.rs:306-408; rust/lance-arrow/src/lib.rs:144-182)

## Repeated-leading-index discrepancy

The binary planner's condition is current==start_idx OR current-last_idx==1, where current is a relative row index and start_idx is a selector ordinal. For a nonempty value of length L and sorted indices [k,k], subtraction gives [0,0]; both iterations satisfy current==start_idx, leaving is_contiguous=true. The chunk reads/copies one value span L, but the output offsets and capacity count two values, reaching the debug assertion L==2L. Release execution reaches fallible array building with inconsistent offsets. This is an explicit source trace, not an executed reproduction. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/binary.rs:251-284; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/binary.rs:309-388)

The dense test includes a repeated later index and checks correct output; it does not include a repeated first index. Its standalone planner uses a 1024-byte threshold, whereas decoder.take uses 64KiB. Do not generalize that passing fixture into all-duplicate correctness or assume the tested standalone plan is the actual take plan. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/binary.rs:616-662)

## Plain bytes, recursive arrays and unsafe boundaries

Plain primitives write values only. Boolean inputs are joined bit by bit and None becomes false; other types use first-array byte_width and each array's offset/length to form an unsafe raw buffer slice. The configured DataType only selects FixedSizeList recursion; the primitive branch otherwise uses the actual first array type. It never validates that every later array has that type or enough bytes for the resulting span. Homogeneous valid Arrow arrays are a safety precondition: mixed narrower arrays can make the computed raw slice exceed its allocation. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/plain.rs:60-152)

Fixed lists recursively write sliced child values, discarding parent and eventual primitive validity. Read reconstructs them with parent validity None; fixed binary reads UInt8 values then builds a width-based array. Signed dimensions are cast and multiplied without local validation. Null primitive payloads are whatever the input values buffer contains, except Boolean's explicit false substitution; the compatibility fixture's zero/null-key expectations do not prove every possible null backing value is zero. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/plain.rs:73-152; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/plain.rs:252-304; rust/lance-file/src/compatibility_tests.rs:100-135)

bytes_to_array requires one value buffer. For FixedWidth, a short response is copied and zero-filled to (len+offset)*width; otherwise aligned Bytes can be retained and misaligned Bytes are copied. The resulting array has null_count0. This means truncated fixed-width input is not necessarily rejected: the active test supplies five bytes for three UInt16 values and expects the missing sixth byte to be zero. Bit-packed Boolean uses its separate buffer branch and starting bit offset. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/plain.rs:174-249; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/plain.rs:575-592; rust/lance-arrow/src/lib.rs:1536-1600)

These codecs perform unchecked pointer/offset/capacity arithmetic and have assertions/downcasts in public-call paths. No local transaction, rollback, flush/shutdown, abort guard or cancellation cleanup appears. Buffered futures preserve order and limit polling concurrency but do not prove backend cancellation; complete IO ownership remains pending. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/binary.rs:48-105; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/binary.rs:309-390; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/plain.rs:90-152; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/plain.rs:325-408; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/dictionary.rs:37-77)

## Dictionary keys and values

DictionaryEncoder supports all eight signed/unsigned integer key widths. It extracts each array's keys and writes them with PlainEncoder; no value comparison, dictionary merge/remap, value persistence or key-validity bitmap occurs. Supplying different dictionaries with the same key width therefore requires the caller to have already established compatible key meaning. The constructor's configured key type controls downcasts; unsupported types return Schema and supported types with an empty slice assert. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/dictionary.rs:26-77)

DictionaryDecoder reads keys using PlainDecoder, clones the shared values Arc and calls DictionaryArray::try_new. Its declared dictionary value type is never compared with the supplied array; result value type follows that array. Keys lose stored validity through plain reconstruction, but dictionary values can independently be null. The one local test writes keys directly using PlainEncoder and never invokes DictionaryEncoder. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/dictionary.rs:104-174; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/dictionary.rs:187-252)

The foundation's binary-like predicate includes views, but both concrete binary encode and facade decode reject them. PlainEncoder can write fixed-width numeric buffers beyond integer widths, whereas schema dictionary hydration explicitly accepts only eight integer value types or the four binary families. These are different boundaries; do not infer symmetric hydration from write dispatch. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/binary.rs:91-105; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/plain.rs:90-115; rust/lance-arrow/src/lib.rs:144-182; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding.rs:116-175)

## Responsibility, visibility and dependencies

This synchronous module reduces borrowed Arrow arrays to a StatisticsRow, accumulates rows in per-field builders, and finishes one Arrow RecordBatch. It does not perform IO, serialize pages, schedule tasks, select file versions or enforce writer rollback. Pub declarations are enclosed by private writer::statistics, without a public re-export here. Arrow supplies arrays/builders, DataFusion ScalarValue stores typed bounds, Lance Field/Schema identifies columns, num_traits supplies numeric bounds and Float operations, and BTreeMap orders output by original field ID. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/writer/statistics.rs:6-34) (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/writer/statistics.rs:611-670) (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/writer/mod.rs:4-4)

## Three separate type boundaries

| Boundary | Accepted types |
|---|---|
| collect_statistics | Boolean; eight integers; Float32/64; Date32/64; valid Time32/64 units; all Timestamp/Duration units; Decimal128; Binary/LargeBinary; Utf8/LargeUtf8; FixedSizeBinary; Dictionary with eight integer key types |
| supports_stats_collection / automatic collector | Boolean; eight integers; Float32/64; Date32/64; Decimal128; Binary/LargeBinary; Utf8/LargeUtf8 |
| StatisticsBuilder::append | Automatic set plus valid Time32/64, Timestamp and Duration; no FixedSizeBinary or Dictionary arm |

The dispatcher panics for an empty outer slice and reaches unreachable for unsupported types, while append uses todo! for unmatched stored dtype. Neither collect_statistics nor StatisticsBuilder::append returns a validation Result for mismatched input arrays or supplied bound scalar types; collector finish separately returns a Result for final batch construction. An empty eligible schema returns None from try_new. Commented list/FixedSizeBinary arms and Decimal256 TODOs are not support. ## Reduction contracts

| Family | No valid ordered values | Ordinary bounds and null counting |
|---|---|---|
| Integers / temporal / Decimal128 | Present native MIN/MAX | Strict native partial comparisons; sum physical array nulls; first dtype carries temporal parameters; Decimal128 first precision/scale |
| Float32/64 | Present -infinity/+infinity | Ignore NaN for extrema without counting it as null; normalize zero minimum to negative zero and maximum to positive zero |
| Boolean | Present false/true | Presence flags; later arrays still add null counts after both values found |
| UTF8 / binary | Typed absent bounds | Lexical prefixes up to64 bytes; optional upper successor when any input was truncated |
| Fixed binary | Absent bounds tagged original width | Prefix payload up to64 bytes but original width retained in both scalar tags; excluded from collector |
| Dictionary | Determined by value reducer | Scan full dictionary values, including unused entries; null count concerns values arrays, not keys/decoded rows; shared dictionaries are rescanned |

These are source contracts, not results of executing Arrow/DataFusion dependencies. Native decimal extrema are not clamped to precision, and primitive scalar conversion can impose separate failures. ## Prefixes, successors and cost

BINARY_PREFIX_LENGTH is64 bytes. UTF8 truncation scans backward over the original string for the longest nonempty prefix ending at or before64. Binary truncation takes exactly64 bytes. The comments saying less than are weaker than the actual <= condition. Values exactly64 bytes are not truncated. Each string/binary reduction has one global flag: if ANY value was truncated, the selected maximum is incremented even if that maximum was short. A missing successor produces a null upper bound. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/writer/statistics.rs:176-387)

Binary increment carries right-to-left, zeroing overflowed suffix bytes; all0xFF returns None. UTF8 increment instead tries successive larger bytes at each position, validates the full candidate, and restores the original byte on overflow before moving left. It keeps suffix bytes and total length unchanged. None is an algorithm limitation, not a proof that no upper bound with another length exists. Prefix comparison/storage is bounded, but UTF8 truncation can traverse a long suffix; reduction scans all valid values except Boolean arrays after both values are known. # Batch task alignment and system columns

Complete local scope: all 1,887 lines of utils/stream.rs. [Table](rust-lance-table.md) · [Exact file and ranges](../L2-files/rust/lance-table/src/utils/stream.rs.md) · [Benchmarks](archive/rust-lance-table-benchmarks.md) · [Contracts](../L3-symbols/behavior-contracts.md) · [Scenarios](../L4-crosscutting/scenarios.md).

This public utils::stream module aligns column streams and attaches row IDs, physical addresses and version arrays to already scheduled batches. It applies physical deletions by filtering or by nulling ID/address columns. It opens no files, spawns no tasks and chooses no downstream concurrency limit. Two fragment call sites merge reader streams, merge overlays, construct the configuration, wrap system columns, then begin projection reordering; complete FragmentReader orchestration remains pending. ## Alignment and shared future lifecycle

MergeStream keeps one pending chunk from each input. It emits the minimum remaining count, splitting bigger chunks with shared futures and Arrow slices. A whole unsplit task moves its original future directly. Split errors become Wrapped with the original Error reachable through SharedReadError::source. Input task order determines column merge order; FuturesOrdered yields component results in that order. Any input stream ending stops the merge without checking remaining totals. Zero-row tasks are allowed. (rust/lance-table/src/utils/stream.rs:41-216)

The outer stream does not await batch data; emitted futures perform the actual merge. Dropping one split future does not itself invalidate another shared handle, and retained slices can retain the whole source batch. Declared sizes must match actual data or slicing can panic; equal actual lengths are checked by RecordBatchExt::merge. Matching field names are not simple concatenation: nested structures may merge and other conflicts keep the left column. Left schema metadata survives. Certain nested-list merge branches can panic; those dependency internals are only contextually read, not fully analyzed. (rust/lance-table/src/utils/stream.rs:90-159; rust/lance-arrow/src/lib.rs:657-677; rust/lance-arrow/src/lib.rs:1231-1332)

## Ordered expansion, read-ahead and schema reuse

The wrapper chooses dense versus ordinary row-ID cursor expansion once, then expands IDs and multi-run versions while pulling tasks in order. Batch futures may complete concurrently without sharing mutable cursors. Metadata Results are captured in those futures: an input batch error propagates first and can mask a precomputed metadata error. Work done while pulling can be discarded if a future is never consumed. (rust/lance-table/src/utils/stream.rs:648-691; rust/lance-table/src/utils/stream.rs:692-848)

Uniform nonzero task sizes enable a 65,536-row read-ahead target and shared output-schema cache. Chunks are aligned to whole batches, capped by selected rows left; a larger task can exceed the target. A nonfinal size change permanently disables both fast paths after draining any usable cached ID chunk. Zero-size tasks do not alter the inferred size; a different final size is allowed. A batch straddling chunks copies its prefix and suffix; fitting slices share storage. Retained output futures/batches can hold multiple old buffers, so the current chunk is not a global memory cap. (rust/lance-table/src/utils/stream.rs:378-405; rust/lance-table/src/utils/stream.rs:692-798)

The OnceLock caches the first completing batch's input/output schemas. Pointer-identical or structurally equal later schemas reuse its output Arc; differing schemas receive a fresh schema without replacing the cache. This path appends fields directly. The incremental fallback instead calls try_with_column repeatedly, which explicitly rejects duplicate names. Do not assume identical malformed-input behavior for both assembly paths. (rust/lance-table/src/utils/stream.rs:592-634; rust/lance-arrow/src/lib.rs:643-648; rust/lance-arrow/src/schema.rs:146-157)

## Selection, errors and deletion semantics

Selection offsets count rows in the requested selection, while ranges/indices identify physical positions in the sequence. Helpers slice params then often unwrap Results, so invalid selection can panic despite a Result-returning public transformer. ReadBatchParams materializers use raw index values and unchecked u32 endpoint conversions; the local total count is primarily a read-ahead estimate. The wrapper checks decoded stable-ID count and returns named CorruptFile on truncation. The direct fallback lacks that exact chunk check. (rust/lance-table/src/utils/stream.rs:266-315; rust/lance-table/src/utils/stream.rs:407-545; rust/lance-io/src/lib.rs:156-219; rust/lance-io/src/lib.rs:248-277)

A one-run version sequence repeats its value without validating the run length against selection. Its O(1) comment concerns locating a version, not allocating/filling the output vector. Multi-run streaming reuses version cursors; direct calls create a new cursor and repeat selection construction. System columns appear in ID, address, last-updated, created order after payload. (rust/lance-table/src/utils/stream.rs:266-315; rust/lance-table/src/utils/stream.rs:553-591; rust/lance-table/src/utils/stream.rs:681-690)

Deletion predicates use physical addresses regardless of stable IDs. Some(NoDeletions) is normalized away. Filter mode removes rows from every column; null mode keeps physical length and combines existing validity with deletion validity only for _rowid/_rowaddr. Payload and version values remain present under deleted rows. If no ID/address field is present, null mode has no identifying null output; test code treats that as an upstream-invalid configuration, but production code does not reject it. Empty filtered batches are returned. (rust/lance-table/src/utils/stream.rs:218-264; rust/lance-table/src/utils/stream.rs:479-551; rust/lance-table/src/utils/stream.rs:636-640; rust/lance-table/src/utils/stream.rs:1517-1526)

## Tests and boundaries

Fixtures cover aligned and differing-boundary merges, sparse IDs with deletion-preserved addresses, unsorted/repeated selection, shared read-ahead buffers, zero tasks, truncated IDs, variable-size fallback, equivalent-schema reuse, physical selection forms, a deletion matrix, one/many-run versions, backwards version selections and direct fallback. They use in-memory ready tasks and buffered consumers; no actual IO or forced delayed completion is present. They do not cover unequal total streams, split-error fanout, declared/actual length mismatches, duplicate system names, malformed uniform version length, or null-only deletion with version columns. Tests were read, not run. (rust/lance-table/src/utils/stream.rs:850-1887)

L4-crosscutting/navigation-index.md: # Ordered development navigation Use one task/read set at a time. Each set contains at most five unique source files, ordered from contract/definition toward mechanism. A broad change spanning multiple mechanisms is split into named subtasks. These are implementation reading routes, not guarantees that a future patch touches only these files. Source ranges refer to the pinned ledger snapshot. Completed crates link directly to frozen L2; ordinary files remain mapped. [Public APIs](../L3-symbols/public-api.md) · [Format](../L3-symbols/format-spec.md) · [Cookbook](cookbook.md) · [Scenarios](scenarios.md) · [Trust/scope](../V21-PROTOCOL.md) ## Primary task routes The explicit engine/API routes above the retained local mechanisms are supplied in the task table below. Read a route's canonical contract before opening its listed files. ### Read and execute a query [Contract and executable trace](../L0-orientation.md#read-path). Read in this order: 1. `rust/lance/src/dataset.rs:1687-1704` — construct snapshot Scanner. 2. `rust/lance/src/dataset/scanner.rs:2632-2675,3210-3375` — validate, choose source, build/execute plan. 3. `rust/lance-datafusion/src/exec.rs:721-761` — partition/order handling. 4. [Frozen reader](../L2-files/rust/lance-file/src/reader.rs.md) → `rust/lance-file/src/reader.rs:740-1028` — persisted metadata to prepared file reads. ### Create or append a dataset [Write contract](../L0-orientation.md#write-path) and [ambiguous outcomes](../L3-symbols/protocol-commit.md#errors-retries-and-ambiguous-success). 1. `rust/lance/src/dataset.rs:950-979` — public entry. 2. `rust/lance/src/dataset/write/insert.rs:98-315` — write/stage versus commit, operation intent. 3. `rust/lance/src/dataset/write.rs:1724-1830` — fragment-writer handoff. 4. `rust/lance/src/dataset/write/commit.rs:294-571` — new/existing/detached dispatch and returned snapshot. 5. `rust/lance/src/io/commit.rs:1581-1937` — existing-table publication and recovery. Status: analyzed at the file's own layer; implementation behavior outside this file is not implied. SHA-256: `a26c12e744f20c4b3fa1e22a394c8394f6186a017dfed01a245ccfcb6a881145`. Reviewed physical lines: 1-852.

## Role and visibility

Public frozen V1 fixed-stride encoder/decoder and private byte conversion and take-chunk helpers. Writes raw primitive buffers, packs booleans across batches, recursively flattens fixed-size lists and reconstructs arrays without stored validity. Contains nine active tests, two helpers and three entirely commented-out historical tests. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/plain.rs:1-852)

## Complete range analysis

### Lines 1-31

SPDX and module prose describe fixed-stride direct storage and O(1) access. That complexity describes computing a row byte position, not total IO, recursive reconstruction or take allocation. Imports provide raw slices, Arrow arithmetic/layout/buffers/selection, async recursion, ordered streams, local Arrow extensions and Reader/Writer. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/plain.rs:1-31)

### Lines 32-59

PlainEncoder stores borrowed Writer and configured DataType; new performs no validation. Static write records tell, returns that position without encoding for an empty array slice, otherwise chooses the first array type and encodes. Instance encode delegates recursively even for an empty slice and can reach an assertion. Its comment calls the return a metadata offset, but primitive implementation returns the raw values start; no separate plain metadata is emitted. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/plain.rs:32-59)

### Lines 60-72

encode_internal branches only on configured FixedSizeList, delegating its item Field; every other configured type goes to encode_primitive, which reads the actual first input type. async_recursion boxes recursive calls. This distinction explains why DictionaryEncoder can configure a dictionary type while passing primitive key arrays. No general configured-vs-actual type check exists. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/plain.rs:60-72)

### Lines 73-89

encode_boolean reserves summed logical length, iterates every input value, replaces None with false and appends values to one BooleanBuilder. It writes only the finished values bitmap, eliminating byte-padding gaps between short arrays. No validity bitmap is written, so null booleans read as valid false. Allocation and iteration are proportional to total input rows. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/plain.rs:73-89)

### Lines 90-117

encode_primitive asserts a nonempty slice and captures writer position. Boolean inputs are downcast and packed; other inputs use the first type's byte_width for every raw buffer slice, starting at each array offset and writing len*width bytes. No endian conversion, validity, per-array type/buffer-length check, alignment padding or rollback. Unsafe from_raw_parts requires each computed span to remain inside a valid allocation across await; mixed narrower arrays can violate that safety precondition. Existing Arrow validity alone does not establish homogeneous inputs. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/plain.rs:90-117)

### Lines 118-154

encode_fixed_size_list downcasts each input or returns Schema with actual type, slices its child values from value_offset(0) for len*value_length, collects shared child arrays and recurses using configured items.data_type. Parent nulls are discarded, as are child validity buffers once primitive encoding occurs. Actual list sizes and configured item type are not compared here; casts/products and recursion depth are unchecked. A failure can follow already-written data in nested/earlier operations. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/plain.rs:118-154)

### Lines 155-173

PlainDecoder privately borrows Reader and DataType and stores position/length. get_byte_range maps booleans to floor(start/8)..ceil(end/8), otherwise multiplies endpoints by byte_width. All byte-offset arithmetic is unchecked. The locally defined DataTypeExt::byte_width panics when width is unavailable; FixedSizeList<Boolean> has no scalar byte width for the take planner (rust/lance-arrow/src/lib.rs:144-182). (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/plain.rs:155-173)

### Lines 174-201

bytes_to_array requires Arrow layout.buffers.len()==1 or returns Internal with type. FixedWidth computes (len+offset).saturating_mul(width); a short Bytes response is copied into that minimum size with zero fill, otherwise BufferExt may retain aligned Bytes or copy misaligned bytes. Non-FixedWidth layouts copy from the byte slice. The len+offset addition itself is unchecked; this helper does not reject truncation for fixed-width values. BufferExt behavior is established at rust/lance-arrow/src/lib.rs:1536-1600. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/plain.rs:174-201)

### Lines 202-225

ArrayDataBuilder constructs the declared type with requested len/offset, null_count0 and one value buffer, then fallibly builds and make_array returns an ArrayRef. All restored rows are valid at this layer. Public PlainDecoder::new returns Result but unconditionally constructs Ok and does not enforce fixed stride, positive dimensions, file bounds or schema compatibility. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/plain.rs:202-225)

### Lines 226-251

  360 |         // If contiguous, continue
  361 |         if indices[i + 1] == indices[i] + 1 {
  362 |             continue;
  363 |         }
  364 |         if indices[i + 1] as usize * byte_width > indices[start] as usize * byte_width + block_size
  365 |         {
  366 |             chunked_ranges.push(start..i + 1);
  367 |             start = i + 1;
  368 |         }
  369 |     }
  370 |     chunked_ranges.push(start..indices.len());
  371 |     chunked_ranges
  372 | }

  374 | impl PlainDecoder<'_> {
  375 |     pub async fn decode(&self) -> Result<ArrayRef> {
  376 |         self.get(0..self.length).await
  377 |     }
  378 | 
  379 |     pub async fn take(&self, indices: &UInt32Array) -> Result<ArrayRef> {
  380 |         if indices.is_empty() {
  381 |             return Ok(new_empty_array(self.data_type));
  382 |         }
  383 | 
  384 |         if matches!(self.data_type, DataType::Boolean) {
  385 |             return self.take_boolean(indices).await;
  386 |         }
  387 | 
  388 |         let block_size = self.reader.block_size();
  389 |         let byte_width = self.data_type.byte_width();
  390 | 
  391 |         let chunked_ranges = make_chunked_requests(indices.values(), byte_width, block_size);
  392 | 
  393 |         let arrays = stream::iter(chunked_ranges)
  394 |             .map(|cr| async move {
  395 |                 let request = indices.slice(cr.start, cr.len());
  396 | 
  397 |                 let start = request.value(0);
  398 |                 let end = request.value(request.len() - 1);
  399 |                 let array = self.get(start as usize..end as usize + 1).await?;
  400 |                 let adjusted_offsets = sub(&request, &UInt32Array::new_scalar(start))?;
  401 |                 Ok::<ArrayRef, Error>(take(&array, &adjusted_offsets, None)?)
  402 |             })
  403 |             .buffered(self.reader.io_parallelism())
  404 |             .try_collect::<Vec<_>>()
  405 |             .await?;
  406 |         let references = arrays.iter().map(|a| a.as_ref()).collect::<Vec<_>>();
  407 |         Ok(concat(&references)?)
  408 |     }
  409 | 
  410 |     #[async_recursion]
  411 |     async fn decode_range(&self, index: Range<usize>) -> Result<ArrayRef> {
  412 |         if index.is_empty() {
  413 |             return Ok(new_empty_array(self.data_type));
  414 |         }
  415 |         match self.data_type {
  416 |             DataType::FixedSizeList(items, list_size) => {
  417 |                 self.decode_fixed_size_list(items, *list_size, index.start, index.end)
  418 |                     .await
  419 |             }
  420 |             DataType::FixedSizeBinary(stride) => {
  421 |                 self.decode_fixed_size_binary(*stride, index.start, index.end)
  422 |                     .await
  423 |             }
  424 |             _ => self.decode_primitive(index.start, index.end).await,
  425 |         }
  426 |     }
  427 | 
  428 |     pub async fn get(&self, params: impl Into<ReadBatchParams>) -> Result<ArrayRef> {
  429 |         match params.into() {
  430 |             ReadBatchParams::Range(range) => self.decode_range(range).await,
  431 |             ReadBatchParams::Ranges(_) => Err(Error::invalid_input(
  432 |                 "multiple ranges are not supported by v1 plain encoding",
  433 |             )),
  434 |             ReadBatchParams::RangeFull => self.decode_range(0..self.length).await,
  435 |             ReadBatchParams::RangeTo(range) => self.decode_range(0..range.end).await,
  436 |             ReadBatchParams::RangeFrom(range) => self.decode_range(range.start..self.length).await,
  437 |             ReadBatchParams::Indices(indices) => self.take(&indices).await,
  438 |         }
  439 |     }
  440 | }

  176 | /// Truncate a UTF8 slice to the longest prefix that is still a valid UTF8 string, while being less than `length` bytes.
  177 | fn truncate_utf8(data: &str, length: usize) -> Option<&str> {
  178 |     // We return values like that at an earlier stage in the process.
  179 |     assert!(data.len() >= length);
  180 |     let mut char_indices = data.char_indices();
  181 | 
  182 |     // We know `data` is a valid UTF8 encoded string, which means it has at least one valid UTF8 byte, which will make this loop exist.
  183 |     while let Some((idx, c)) = char_indices.next_back() {
  184 |         let split_point = idx + c.len_utf8();
  185 |         if split_point <= length {
  186 |             return Some(&data[0..split_point]);
  187 |         }
  188 |     }
  189 | 
  190 |     None
  191 | }

  193 | /// Try and increment the string's bytes from right to left, returning when the result is a valid UTF8 string.
  194 | /// Returns `None` when it can't increment any byte.
  195 | fn increment_utf8(mut data: Vec<u8>) -> Option<Vec<u8>> {
  196 |     for idx in (0..data.len()).rev() {
  197 |         let original = data[idx];
  198 |         let (mut byte, mut overflow) = data[idx].overflowing_add(1);
  199 | 
  200 |         // Until overflow: 0xFF -> 0x00
  201 |         while !overflow {
  202 |             data[idx] = byte;
  203 | 
  204 |             if str::from_utf8(&data).is_ok() {
  205 |                 return Some(data);
  206 |             }
  207 |             (byte, overflow) = data[idx].overflowing_add(1);
  208 |         }
  209 | 
  210 |         data[idx] = original;
  211 |     }
  212 | 
  213 |     None
  214 | }

  228 | fn increment(mut data: Vec<u8>) -> Option<Vec<u8>> {

  232 | 
  233 |         if !overflow {
  234 |             return Some(data);
  235 |         }
  236 |     }
  237 |

  521 |         DataType::Timestamp(TimeUnit::Second, _) => get_statistics::<TimestampSecondType>(arrays),

  525 |         DataType::Timestamp(TimeUnit::Microsecond, _) => {

  528 |         DataType::Timestamp(TimeUnit::Nanosecond, _) => {

  531 |         DataType::Time64(TimeUnit::Microsecond) => get_statistics::<Time64MicrosecondType>(arrays),

  550 | pub fn collect_statistics(arrays: &[&ArrayRef]) -> StatisticsRow {
  551 |     if arrays.is_empty() {
  552 |         panic!("No arrays to collect statistics from");
  553 |     }
  554 |     match arrays[0].data_type() {
  555 |         DataType::Boolean => get_boolean_statistics(arrays),
  556 |         DataType::Int8 => get_statistics::<Int8Type>(arrays),
  557 |         DataType::UInt8 => get_statistics::<UInt8Type>(arrays),
  558 |         DataType::Int16 => get_statistics::<Int16Type>(arrays),
  559 |         DataType::UInt16 => get_statistics::<UInt16Type>(arrays),
  560 |         DataType::Int32 => get_statistics::<Int32Type>(arrays),
  561 |         DataType::UInt32 => get_statistics::<UInt32Type>(arrays),
  562 |         DataType::Int64 => get_statistics::<Int64Type>(arrays),
  563 |         DataType::UInt64 => get_statistics::<UInt64Type>(arrays),
  564 |         DataType::Float32 => get_float_statistics::<Float32Type>(arrays),
  565 |         DataType::Float64 => get_float_statistics::<Float64Type>(arrays),
  566 |         DataType::Date32
  567 |         | DataType::Time32(_)
  568 |         | DataType::Date64
  569 |         | DataType::Time64(_)
  570 |         | DataType::Timestamp(_, _)
  571 |         | DataType::Duration(_) => get_temporal_statistics(arrays),
  572 |         DataType::Decimal128(_, _) => get_decimal_statistics(arrays),
  573 |         // TODO: Decimal256
  574 |         DataType::Binary => get_binary_statistics::<i32>(arrays),
  575 |         DataType::LargeBinary => get_binary_statistics::<i64>(arrays),
  576 |         DataType::FixedSizeBinary(_) => get_fixed_size_binary_statistics(arrays),
  577 |         DataType::Utf8 => get_string_statistics::<i32>(arrays),
  578 |         DataType::LargeUtf8 => get_string_statistics::<i64>(arrays),
  579 |         DataType::Dictionary(_, _) => get_dictionary_statistics(arrays),
  580 |         // DataType::List(_) => get_list_statistics(arrays),
  581 |         // DataType::LargeList(_) => get_list_statistics(arrays),
  582 |         _ => unreachable!(),
  583 |     }
  584 | }

  611 | #[derive(Debug)]
  612 | pub struct StatisticsCollector {
  613 |     builders: BTreeMap<i32, (Field, StatisticsBuilder)>,
  614 | }
  615 | 
  616 | impl StatisticsCollector {
  617 |     /// Try to create a new statistics collection. If no fields in the schema
  618 |     /// support statistics, will just return None.
  619 |     pub fn try_new(schema: &Schema) -> Option<Self> {
  620 |         let builders: BTreeMap<i32, (Field, StatisticsBuilder)> = visit_fields(schema)
  621 |             .filter(|f| supports_stats_collection(&f.data_type()))
  622 |             .map(|f| (f.id, (f.clone(), StatisticsBuilder::new(&f.data_type()))))
  623 |             .collect();
  624 |         if builders.is_empty() {
  625 |             None
  626 |         } else {
  627 |             Some(Self { builders })
  628 |         }
  629 |     }
  630 | 
  631 |     pub fn get_builder(&mut self, field_id: i32) -> Option<&mut StatisticsBuilder> {
  632 |         self.builders.get_mut(&field_id).map(|(_, b)| b)
  633 |     }
  634 | 
  635 |     pub fn finish(&mut self) -> Result<RecordBatch> {
  636 |         let mut arrays: Vec<ArrayRef> = vec![];
  637 |         let mut fields: Vec<ArrowField> = vec![];
  638 | 
  639 |         self.builders.iter_mut().for_each(|(_, (field, builder))| {
  640 |             let null_count = Arc::new(builder.null_count.finish());
  641 |             let min_value = Arc::new(builder.min_value.finish());
  642 |             let max_value = Arc::new(builder.max_value.finish());
  643 |             let struct_fields = vec![
  644 |                 ArrowField::new("null_count", DataType::Int64, false),
  645 |                 // Bounds can be absent for empty pages regardless of the data field's
  646 |                 // nullability.
  647 |                 ArrowField::new("min_value", field.data_type(), true),
  648 |                 ArrowField::new("max_value", field.data_type(), true),
  649 |             ];
  650 | 
  651 |             let stats = StructArray::new(
  652 |                 struct_fields.clone().into(),
  653 |                 vec![null_count.clone(), min_value, max_value],
  654 |                 null_count.nulls().cloned(),
  655 |             );
  656 |             let field = ArrowField::new_struct(field.id.to_string(), struct_fields, false);
  657 |             fields.push(field);
  658 |             arrays.push(Arc::new(stats));
  659 |         });
  660 | 
  661 |         let schema = Arc::new(ArrowSchema::new(fields));
  662 |         let batch = RecordBatch::try_new(schema, arrays);
  663 |         match batch {
  664 |             Ok(batch) => Ok(batch),
  665 |             _ => Err(ArrowError::SchemaError(
  666 |                 "all columns in a record batch must have the same length".to_string(),
  667 |             )
  668 |             .into()),
  669 |         }
  670 |     }
  671 | }
  672 | 
  673 | /// Visit all fields, only visiting children of structs.
  674 | fn visit_fields(schema: &Schema) -> impl Iterator<Item = &Field> {
  675 |     let mut fields: Vec<&Field> = schema.fields.iter().rev().collect();
  676 |     std::iter::from_fn(move || {
  677 |         if let Some(field) = fields.pop() {
  678 |             if field.data_type().is_struct() {
  679 |                 fields.extend(field.children.iter().rev());
  680 |             }
  681 |             Some(field)
  682 |         } else {
  683 |             None
  684 |         }
  685 |     })
  686 | }

  808 |     fn statistics_appender<T: arrow_array::ArrowPrimitiveType>(&mut self, row: StatisticsRow) {
  809 |         let min_value_builder = self
  810 |             .min_value
  811 |             .as_any_mut()
  812 |             .downcast_mut::<PrimitiveBuilder<T>>()
  813 |             .unwrap();
  814 |         let max_value_builder = self
  815 |             .max_value
  816 |             .as_any_mut()
  817 |             .downcast_mut::<PrimitiveBuilder<T>>()
  818 |             .unwrap();
  819 | 
  820 |         let min_value = row
  821 |             .min_value
  822 |             .to_array()
  823 |             .unwrap()
  824 |             .as_any()
  825 |             .downcast_ref::<PrimitiveArray<T>>()
  826 |             .unwrap()
  827 |             .value(0);
  828 |         let max_value = row
  829 |             .max_value
  830 |             .to_array()
  831 |             .unwrap()
  832 |             .as_any()
  833 |             .downcast_ref::<PrimitiveArray<T>>()
  834 |             .unwrap()
  835 |             .value(0);
  836 | 
  837 |         self.null_count.append_value(row.null_count);
  838 |         min_value_builder.append_value(min_value);
  839 |         max_value_builder.append_value(max_value);

  218 | /// Apply a mask to the batch, where rows are "deleted" by the _rowid column null.
  219 | ///
  220 | /// This is used partly as a performance optimization (cheaper to null than to filter)
  221 | /// but also because there are cases where we want to load the physical rows.  For example,
  222 | /// we may be replacing a column based on some UDF and we want to provide a value for the
  223 | /// deleted rows to ensure the fragments are aligned.
  224 | fn apply_deletions_as_nulls(batch: RecordBatch, mask: &BooleanArray) -> Result<RecordBatch> {
  225 |     // Transform mask into null buffer. Null means deleted, though note that
  226 |     // null buffers are actually validity buffers, so True means not null
  227 |     // and thus not deleted.
  228 |     let mask_buffer = NullBuffer::new(mask.values().clone());
  229 | 
  230 |     if mask_buffer.null_count() == 0 {
  231 |         // No rows are deleted
  232 |         return Ok(batch);
  233 |     }
  234 | 
  235 |     // For each column convert to data
  236 |     let new_columns = batch
  237 |         .schema()
  238 |         .fields()
  239 |         .iter()
  240 |         .zip(batch.columns())
  241 |         .map(|(field, col)| {
  242 |             if field.name() == ROW_ID || field.name() == ROW_ADDR {
  243 |                 let col_data = col.to_data();
  244 |                 // If it already has a validity bitmap, then AND it with the mask.
  245 |                 // Otherwise, use the boolean buffer as the mask.
  246 |                 let null_buffer = NullBuffer::union(col_data.nulls(), Some(&mask_buffer));
  247 | 
  248 |                 Ok(col_data
  249 |                     .into_builder()
  250 |                     .null_bit_buffer(null_buffer.map(|b| b.buffer().clone()))
  251 |                     .build()
  252 |                     .map(make_array)?)
  253 |             } else {
  254 |                 Ok(col.clone())
  255 |             }
  256 |         })
  257 |         .collect::<Result<Vec<_>>>()?;
  258 | 
  259 |     Ok(RecordBatch::try_new_with_options(
  260 |         batch.schema(),
  261 |         new_columns,
  262 |         &RecordBatchOptions::new().with_row_count(Some(batch.num_rows())),
  263 |     )?)
  264 | }

  527 |                 .to_ranges()
  528 |                 .unwrap();
  529 |             let row_ids = row_id_sequence
  530 |                 .select(
  531 |                     selection
  532 |                         .iter()
  533 |                         .flat_map(|r| r.start as usize..r.end as usize),
  534 |                 )
  535 |                 .collect::<UInt64Array>();
  536 |             Some(Arc::new(row_ids))
  537 |         } else {
  538 |             // If we don't have a row id sequence, can assume the row ids are
  539 |             // the same as the row addresses.
  540 |             row_addrs.clone()
  541 |         }
  542 |     } else {
  543 |         None
  544 |     };
  545 | 
  546 |     let span = tracing::span!(tracing::Level::DEBUG, "apply_deletions");
  547 |     let _enter = span.enter();
  548 |     let deletion_mask = deletion_vector.and_then(|v| {
  549 |         let row_addrs: &[u64] = row_addrs.as_ref().unwrap().values();
  550 |         v.build_predicate(row_addrs.iter())
  551 |     });
  552 | 
  553 |     let mut system_columns: Vec<(Field, ArrayRef)> = Vec::with_capacity(4);
  554 |     if config.with_row_id {
  555 |         system_columns.push((ROW_ID_FIELD.clone(), row_ids.unwrap()));
  556 |     }
  557 |     if config.with_row_addr {
  558 |         system_columns.push((ROW_ADDR_FIELD.clone(), row_addrs.unwrap()));
  559 |     }
  560 |     if config.with_row_last_updated_at_version {
  561 |         let version_arr = if let Some(version_arr) = last_updated_versions {
  562 |             version_arr?
  563 |         } else if let Some(sequence) = &config.last_updated_at_sequence {
  564 |             Arc::new(UInt64Array::from(version_values_for_selection(
  565 |                 sequence,
  566 |                 &config.params,
  567 |                 batch_offset,
  568 |                 num_rows,
  569 |             )?))
  570 |         } else {
  571 |             // Default to version 1 if sequence not provided
  572 |             Arc::new(UInt64Array::from(vec![1u64; num_rows as usize]))
  573 |         };
  574 |         system_columns.push((ROW_LAST_UPDATED_AT_VERSION_FIELD.clone(), version_arr));
  575 |     }
  576 |     if config.with_row_created_at_version {
  577 |         let version_arr = if let Some(version_arr) = created_versions {
  578 |             version_arr?
  579 |         } else if let Some(sequence) = &config.created_at_sequence {
  580 |             Arc::new(UInt64Array::from(version_values_for_selection(
  581 |                 sequence,
  582 |                 &config.params,
  583 |                 batch_offset,
  584 |                 num_rows,
  585 |             )?))
  586 |         } else {
  587 |             // Default to version 1 if sequence not provided
  588 |             Arc::new(UInt64Array::from(vec![1u64; num_rows as usize]))
  589 |         };
  590 |         system_columns.push((ROW_CREATED_AT_VERSION_FIELD.clone(), version_arr));
  591 |     }
  592 | 
  593 |     let batch = if system_columns.is_empty() {
  594 |         batch
  595 |     } else if let Some(output_schema_cache) = output_schema_cache {
  596 |         let input_schema = batch.schema();
  597 |         let make_output_schema = || {
  598 |             let mut fields = input_schema
  599 |                 .fields()
  600 |                 .iter()
  601 |                 .map(|field| field.as_ref().clone())
  602 |                 .collect::<Vec<_>>();
  603 |             fields.extend(system_columns.iter().map(|(field, _)| field.clone()));
  604 |             Arc::new(Schema::new_with_metadata(
  605 |                 fields,
  606 |                 input_schema.metadata().clone(),
  607 |             ))
  608 |         };
  609 |         let cached = output_schema_cache.get_or_init(|| CachedOutputSchema {
  610 |             input: input_schema.clone(),
  611 |             output: make_output_schema(),
  612 |         });
  613 |         let output_schema = if Arc::ptr_eq(&cached.input, &input_schema)
  614 |             || cached.input.as_ref() == input_schema.as_ref()
  615 |         {
  616 |             cached.output.clone()
  617 |         } else {
  618 |             make_output_schema()
  619 |         };
  620 |         let mut columns = Vec::with_capacity(batch.num_columns() + system_columns.len());
  621 |         columns.extend_from_slice(batch.columns());
  622 |         columns.extend(system_columns.into_iter().map(|(_, array)| array));
  623 |         RecordBatch::try_new_with_options(
  624 |             output_schema,
  625 |             columns,
  626 |             &RecordBatchOptions::new().with_row_count(Some(batch.num_rows())),
  627 |         )?
  628 |     } else {
  629 |         system_columns
  630 |             .into_iter()
  631 |             .try_fold(batch, |batch, (field, array)| {
  632 |                 batch.try_with_column(field, array)
  633 |             })?
  634 |     };
  635 | 
  636 |     match (deletion_mask, config.make_deletions_null) {
  637 |         (None, _) => Ok(batch),
  638 |         (Some(mask), false) => Ok(arrow::compute::filter_record_batch(&batch, &mask)?),
  639 |         (Some(mask), true) => Ok(apply_deletions_as_nulls(batch, &mask)?),
  640 |     }
  641 | }

  643 | /// Given a stream of batch tasks this function will add a row ids column (if requested)
  644 | /// and also apply a deletions vector to the batch.
  645 | ///
  646 | /// This converts from BatchTaskStream to BatchFutStream because, if we are applying a
  647 | /// deletion vector, it is impossible to know how many output rows we will have.
  648 | pub fn wrap_with_row_id_and_delete(
  649 |     stream: ReadBatchTaskStream,
  650 |     fragment_id: u32,
  651 |     config: RowIdAndDeletesConfig,
  652 | ) -> ReadBatchFutStream {
  653 |     let (row_id_cursor, use_dense_row_id_expansion) = config
  654 |         .row_id_sequence
  655 |         .as_ref()
  656 |         .filter(|_| config.with_row_id)
  657 |         .map(|sequence| {
  658 |             let (cursor, use_dense_range_expansion) = sequence.cursor_with_dense_range_expansion();
  659 |             (Some(cursor), use_dense_range_expansion)
  660 |         })
  661 |         .unwrap_or((None, false));
  662 |     if use_dense_row_id_expansion {
  663 |         wrap_with_row_id_and_delete_impl::<true>(stream, fragment_id, config, row_id_cursor)
  664 |     } else {
  665 |         wrap_with_row_id_and_delete_impl::<false>(stream, fragment_id, config, row_id_cursor)
  666 |     }
  667 | }
  668 | 
  669 | fn wrap_with_row_id_and_delete_impl<const USE_DENSE_ROW_ID_EXPANSION: bool>(
  670 |     stream: ReadBatchTaskStream,
  671 |     fragment_id: u32,
  672 |     config: RowIdAndDeletesConfig,
  673 |     mut row_id_cursor: Option<RowIdSequenceCursor>,
  674 | ) -> ReadBatchFutStream {
  675 |     let config = Arc::new(config);
  676 |     let output_schema_cache = Arc::new(OnceLock::new());
  677 |     let mut row_id_chunk: Option<PrecomputedRowIdChunk> = None;
  678 |     let mut uniform_batch_size = None;
  679 |     let mut use_uniform_batch_fast_paths = true;
  680 |     let selected_rows = selected_row_count(&config.params, config.total_num_rows as usize);
  681 |     let mut last_updated_cursor = config
  682 |         .last_updated_at_sequence
  683 |         .as_ref()
  684 |         .filter(|sequence| config.with_row_last_updated_at_version && sequence.runs.len() > 1)
  685 |         .map(|sequence| sequence.cursor());
  686 |     let mut created_cursor = config
  687 |         .created_at_sequence
  688 |         .as_ref()
  689 |         .filter(|sequence| config.with_row_created_at_version && sequence.runs.len() > 1)
  690 |         .map(|sequence| sequence.cursor());
  691 |     let mut offset = 0;
  692 |     stream
  693 |         .map(move |batch_task| {
  694 |             let config = config.clone();
  695 |             let this_offset = offset;
  696 |             let num_rows = batch_task.num_rows;
  697 |             offset += num_rows;
  698 |             let logical_offset = this_offset as usize;
  699 |             let num_rows_usize = num_rows as usize;
  700 |             if num_rows_usize != 0 && use_uniform_batch_fast_paths {
  701 |                 if let Some(batch_size) = uniform_batch_size {
  702 |                     // A shorter final batch is expected. Any other task-size change can
  703 |                     // repeatedly straddle read-ahead boundaries. Drain the current row-ID
  704 |                     // cache, then use exact per-task decoding and the original incremental
  705 |                     // system-column assembly from this point forward.
  706 |                     if num_rows_usize != batch_size
  707 |                         && logical_offset + num_rows_usize < selected_rows
  708 |                     {
  709 |                         use_uniform_batch_fast_paths = false;
  710 |                     }
  711 |                 } else {
  712 |                     uniform_batch_size = Some(num_rows_usize);
  713 |                 }
  714 |             }
  715 |             let output_schema_cache = use_uniform_batch_fast_paths
  716 |                 .then(|| output_schema_cache.clone());
  717 |             // Build row ids while pulling the ordered task stream, before the
  718 |             // batch futures can run concurrently. Adjacent batches share a
  719 |             // bounded chunk and take zero-copy Arrow slices from it.
  720 |             let row_ids = config.row_id_sequence.as_ref().and_then(|sequence| {
  721 |                 row_id_cursor.as_mut().map(|cursor| {
  722 |                     if num_rows_usize == 0 {
  723 |                         return Ok(Arc::new(UInt64Array::from(Vec::<u64>::new())));
  724 |                     }
  725 |                     if !use_uniform_batch_fast_paths
  726 |                         && row_id_chunk
  727 |                             .as_ref()
  728 |                             .is_none_or(|chunk| chunk.end_offset() <= logical_offset)
  729 |                     {
  730 |                         row_id_chunk = None;
  731 |                         return decode_row_id_chunk::<USE_DENSE_ROW_ID_EXPANSION>(
  732 |                             sequence,
  733 |                             cursor,
  734 |                             &config.params,
  735 |                             logical_offset,
  736 |                             num_rows_usize,
  737 |                         )
  738 |                         .map(|chunk| chunk.values);
  739 |                     }
  740 |                     if let Some(row_ids) = row_id_chunk
  741 |                         .as_ref()
  742 |                         .and_then(|chunk| chunk.slice(logical_offset, num_rows_usize))
  743 |                     {
  744 |                         return Ok(row_ids);
  745 |                     }
  746 | 
  747 |                     let prefix = row_id_chunk.as_ref().and_then(|chunk| {
  748 |                         let prefix_len = chunk.end_offset().checked_sub(logical_offset)?;
  749 |                         if prefix_len == 0 {
  750 |                             None
  751 |                         } else {
  752 |                             chunk.slice(logical_offset, prefix_len)
  753 |                         }
  754 |                     });
  755 |                     let decode_offset = logical_offset
  756 |                         + prefix
  757 |                             .as_ref()
  758 |                             .map(|row_ids| row_ids.len())
  759 |                             .unwrap_or_default();
  760 |                     let required_end = logical_offset + num_rows_usize;
  761 |                     let missing_rows = required_end.saturating_sub(decode_offset);
  762 |                     let chunk_len = if use_uniform_batch_fast_paths {
  763 |                         let batch_size = uniform_batch_size.unwrap_or(num_rows_usize);
  764 |                         let batches_per_chunk = (ROW_ID_READ_AHEAD_ROWS / batch_size).max(1);
  765 |                         let chunk_rows = batch_size.saturating_mul(batches_per_chunk);
  766 |                         missing_rows.max(chunk_rows)
  767 |                     } else {
  768 |                         missing_rows
  769 |                     }
  770 |                     .min(selected_rows.saturating_sub(decode_offset));
  771 |                     let chunk = decode_row_id_chunk::<USE_DENSE_ROW_ID_EXPANSION>(
  772 |                         sequence,
  773 |                         cursor,
  774 |                         &config.params,
  775 |                         decode_offset,
  776 |                         chunk_len,
  777 |                     )?;
  778 |                     let suffix = chunk.slice(decode_offset, missing_rows).ok_or_else(|| {
  779 |                         Error::corrupt_file_named(
  780 |                             "row ID metadata",
  781 |                             format!(
  782 |                                 "decoded row ID chunk at selected offset {decode_offset} contains {} rows, but the current batch requires {missing_rows} more rows",
  783 |                                 chunk.values.len()
  784 |                             ),
  785 |                         )
  786 |                     })?;
  787 |                     let row_ids = if let Some(prefix) = prefix {
  788 |                         let mut values = Vec::with_capacity(num_rows_usize);
  789 |                         values.extend_from_slice(prefix.values());
  790 |                         values.extend_from_slice(suffix.values());
  791 |                         Arc::new(UInt64Array::from(values))
  792 |                     } else {
  793 |                         suffix
  794 |                     };
  795 |                     row_id_chunk = Some(chunk);
  796 |                     Ok(row_ids)
  797 |                 })
  798 |             });
  799 |             let last_updated_versions =
  800 |                 config
  801 |                     .last_updated_at_sequence
  802 |                     .as_ref()
  803 |                     .and_then(|sequence| {
  804 |                         last_updated_cursor.as_mut().map(|cursor| {
  805 |                             version_values_for_selection_with_cursor(
  806 |                                 sequence,
  807 |                                 cursor,
  808 |                                 &config.params,
  809 |                                 this_offset,
  810 |                                 num_rows,
  811 |                             )
  812 |                             .map(UInt64Array::from)
  813 |                             .map(Arc::new)
  814 |                         })
  815 |                     });
  816 |             let created_versions = config.created_at_sequence.as_ref().and_then(|sequence| {
  817 |                 created_cursor.as_mut().map(|cursor| {
  818 |                     version_values_for_selection_with_cursor(
  819 |                         sequence,
  820 |                         cursor,
  821 |                         &config.params,
  822 |                         this_offset,
  823 |                         num_rows,
  824 |                     )
  825 |                     .map(UInt64Array::from)
  826 |                     .map(Arc::new)
  827 |                 })
  828 |             });
  829 |             batch_task
  830 |                 .task
  831 |                 .map(move |batch| {
  832 |                     apply_row_id_and_deletes_with_system_columns(
  833 |                         batch?,
  834 |                         this_offset,
  835 |                         fragment_id,
  836 |                         config.as_ref(),
  837 |                         PrecomputedSystemColumns {
  838 |                             row_ids,
  839 |                             last_updated_versions,
  840 |                             created_versions,
  841 |                         },
  842 |                         output_schema_cache.as_deref(),
  843 |                     )
  844 |                 })
  845 |                 .boxed()
  846 |         })
  847 |         .boxed()
  848 | }

# Public API contracts and cross-language routes

**V2.1 scope:** contracts for the engine's public families, exact declaration/argument navigation for all direct-source public entries in the five newly mapped subsystems, and retained deep API records for completed crates. The consumer has source access. A declared documentation contract is labeled separately from a behavior checked against implementation. Java and designated peripherals remain mapped only. [Architecture](../L0-orientation.md) · [Python map](../L1-modules/python.md) · [Dataset map](../L1-modules/rust-lance.md).

## Complete declaration routes without a second symbol ledger

| Surface | Contract/signature directory | Decision contract |
|---|---|---|
| Dataset and engine builders/execution extensions | [Rust lance declarations](api-reference/lance.md) | Snapshot/read/write rules below; [commit](protocol-commit.md), [index lifecycle](protocol-index.md) |
| Scalar/vector/FTS index implementations and plugin seams | [lance-index](api-reference/lance-index.md), [lance-index-core](api-reference/lance-index-core.md) | [Plugin, certainty, training, update and query contracts](protocol-index.md) |
| Reader/Writer/ObjectStore/scheduling interfaces | [lance-io](api-reference/lance-io.md) | [I/O ownership and admission](protocol-io.md) |
| Planner, execution, serialization and expression interfaces | [lance-datafusion](api-reference/lance-datafusion.md) | Query plan and integration rules below |
| Python root/package classes, functions, methods, constructors | [Python declarations and root exports](api-reference/python.md) | Facade/native/engine mapping below |
| Core types, schema, errors, memory/cache/identity | [Completed core API catalog](../L1-modules/rust-lance-core.md) | [Frozen production behaviors](behavior-contracts.md), linked L2 records |
| Manifest, operations, commit handlers, row IDs | [Completed table API catalog](../L1-modules/rust-lance-table.md) | [Format](format-spec.md), [transaction orchestration](protocol-commit.md) |
| File readers/writers, exact versions | [Completed file API catalog](../L1-modules/rust-lance-file.md) | [Format gates](format-spec.md) |
| Encoding strategies/codecs/structural types | [Encoding catalog](../L1-modules/rust-lance-encoding.md), [residual map](../L1-modules/peripheral-maps.md) | [Encoding selection](protocol-encoding.md), retained checked ranges |
| Protobuf messages and fields | [Complete schema directory](format-spec.md#complete-field-directory) | Declared wire/persistence contract plus exact runtime gates |
| Java | [Java Module Map](../L1-modules/java.md) | Mapped only; no deep JNI/ABI guarantee |
| Namespaces, numerical/tokenizer/geo helpers, tools and other peripherals | [Peripheral maps](../L1-modules/peripheral-maps.md) | Mapped only; source required for implementation beyond the stated interface |

The six new declaration directories are **navigation artifacts referenced by these contracts**, not additions to frozen `symbols.json`. They retain source-authored first-paragraph documentation and source ranges. Rust `pub` under private/cfg modules is a declaration locator, not a compiler-certified external export; trait members/enum variants are reached through their owner. Python inventories local definitions, not inherited Arrow/Pandas APIs. Undocumented entries explicitly lack a standalone documentation summary; use the family's rules and exact source range instead of inventing behavior. No excluded tests/generated code or dependency implementation was used.

## Dataset ownership, version and mutation

A Dataset represents a checked-out manifest snapshot. `Dataset::open(uri)` loads through DatasetBuilder. Numeric checkout stays on the current branch; a named tag resolves its recorded branch/version. Checkout returns a new Dataset, while `checkout_latest(&mut self)` replaces manifest and derived fragment bitmap; it clears base-store caches if base paths changed. `main` is the default-branch alias in reference contexts. (rust/lance/src/dataset.rs:520-588)

Restore creates a **new** transaction based on the latest version, pointing at the currently checked-out historical version. It is not an in-place rewrite of that historical manifest. Detached commits do not become latest and do not join ordinary history; the builder also enforces existing-dataset/v2-manifest-path requirements. Public commit entry points accept operation/read version/store/handler/session parameters and delegate to the common path. (rust/lance/src/dataset.rs:1459-1474; rust/lance/src/dataset.rs:1620-1669; rust/lance/src/dataset/write/commit.rs:460-513)

Mutation methods have distinct handle effects: Rust builders commonly return a new Dataset/result; `&mut Dataset` convenience methods replace their state after success. Python native delete/update/restore/compaction/index methods replace the internal Arc after successful execution; an existing independently checked-out handle remains its own snapshot. Do not describe every Python method as returning a new Dataset: delete/update return count dictionaries, create_index returns the facade, and uncommitted index creation does not update the snapshot. (python/src/dataset.rs:2006-2098; python/src/dataset.rs:2274-2288; python/src/dataset.rs:2867-2884; python/src/dataset/optimize.rs:509-523; python/python/lance/dataset.py:4575-4606)

Storage mutation is not atomic merely because the public function returns Result: data files can exist before commit, and a storage error can follow successful publication. Use the [commit outcome contract](protocol-commit.md#errors-retries-and-ambiguous-success) before retrying or cleaning files. Cleanup of old versions is separately destructive: removed versions cannot be checked out/restored and their unique data can be lost. The explanation path computes a cleanup plan without deleting files. (rust/lance/src/dataset.rs:1477-1483; python/src/dataset.rs:2291-2338)

## Read/query contracts

Rust `Dataset::scan()` creates a Scanner. `try_into_stream` builds a physical plan and executes it; collecting batches is a separate operation. Plan order is source → filter → sort → limit/offset → late take/projection as required. Source selection and index use depend on search and prefilter options. Invalid combinations fail validation, and requesting projected constants alone is not automatically a supported row-count source. (rust/lance/src/dataset.rs:1687-1704; rust/lance/src/dataset/scanner.rs:2632-2675; rust/lance/src/dataset/scanner.rs:3210-3375)

`take` selects logical row positions; `take_rows` selects internal row IDs. IDs and encoded physical addresses are separate when stable IDs are enabled. Unfiltered count sums fragment counts; a filtered count uses a scanner with empty user projection plus row ID. Python's Arrow-expression count uses its scanner directly, whereas string/None count goes through the native Dataset count method. (rust/lance/src/dataset.rs:1705-1778; python/python/lance/dataset.py:2616-2622; python/src/dataset.rs:1656-1685)

Python scanner defaults are applied before explicit non-None options. The final builder forwards options to the native scanner. Projection by names and projection by SQL transforms are mutually exclusive; string and Substrait filters are also mutually exclusive at the binding. Row-ID/address flags are separate; row-address prefilter bytes use the shared RowAddrMask decoder. FTS phrases cannot target multiple columns in the native dict-query route. (python/python/lance/dataset.py:1496-1565; python/python/lance/dataset.py:7348-7385; python/src/dataset.rs:1232-1437)

`LanceScanner.to_table` materializes the entire reader; `to_batches` iterates it. The native LanceReader owns a background stream producer, cancellation channel and bounded output channel. It terminates on first stream error/end or caller/channel cancellation; an unexpectedly closed producer channel becomes an error rather than silent EOF. Retaining all yielded batches can consume unbounded caller memory even though the channel is bounded. (python/python/lance/dataset.py:7399-7409; python/src/reader.rs:48-123)

DataFusion integration parses/qualifies identifiers according to planner options: exact field-name matching precedes ASCII case-insensitive matching; relation qualification is disabled by default and otherwise dots can represent nested access. The Dataset TableProvider translates projection/filter/limit into Scanner and declares Exact filter pushdown. Multiple output partitions are merged preserving known ordering, otherwise coalesced; a single partition executes directly. Preserve declared pushdown exactness when adding expressions. (rust/lance-datafusion/src/planner.rs:280-350; rust/lance/src/datafusion/dataframe.rs:132-197; rust/lance-datafusion/src/exec.rs:721-761)

## Write, update and index contracts

`Dataset::write` accepts an iterator/stream conversion and InsertBuilder writes fragments before CommitBuilder publishes an Overwrite or Append operation. `execute_uncommitted` returns staged intent/data, not a visible new version. Python `write_dataset` validates/converts its input and destination, then native `_write_dataset` converts a native Scanner or Arrow stream and calls Rust Dataset::write. The binding recognizes case-insensitive create/append/overwrite and rejects other modes. (rust/lance/src/dataset.rs:950-979; rust/lance/src/dataset/write/insert.rs:98-166; rust/lance/src/dataset/write/insert.rs:202-315; python/python/lance/dataset.py:8350-8377; python/src/dataset.rs:4849-4888)

Python delete/update accept SQL or serialize Arrow expressions as Substrait. The native layer rejects predicates of other types, configures retry parameters, and delegates to DeleteBuilder/UpdateBuilder. Update assignments are strings parsed by the Rust builder; input/build errors map to ValueError and operation execution errors to IOError in this route. Returned keys are `num_deleted_rows` and `num_rows_updated`. The [conflict protocol](protocol-commit.md) determines whether operation recomputation is required. (python/python/lance/dataset.py:2938-2943; python/python/lance/dataset.py:3147-3158; python/src/dataset.rs:2006-2098)

Python native index creation uppercases a supported high-level type discriminator. Generic `SCALAR` requires a config carrying its plugin type and serialized parameters, so custom plugin names need not be added as new built-in discriminators. Named FTS parameters are checked against an allowlist. Missing replace/train flags default true here. If fragment_ids are present, native creation uses execute_uncommitted and does not update the Dataset; ordinary creation publishes then replaces the handle. The Python scalar facade explicitly directs distributed forms that require it to create_index_uncommitted. (python/src/dataset.rs:2616-2819; python/src/dataset.rs:2834-2884; python/python/lance/dataset.py:3905-3932)

Compaction has plan → execute tasks → commit phases for distributed use; the convenience execute path performs the whole operation and updates the Python handle. Commit may use a subset of completed task results. Preserve original read versions and deletion/rewrite reconciliation; [L0 compaction](../L0-orientation.md) and [commit lineage](protocol-commit.md#index-coverage-and-rewrite-lineage) explain why the driver must not substitute its newer snapshot for task intent. OptimizeIndices similarly delegates options to DatasetIndexExt and updates the native snapshot after success. (python/src/dataset/optimize.rs:479-523; python/src/dataset/optimize.rs:559-606; python/src/dataset.rs:2587-2613; rust/lance/src/dataset/optimize.rs:3156-3260)

## Python-to-Rust ordered read maps

Each row is an ordered set, normally three to five unique files. The declaration directory contains every local public method and its exact range, including ancillary families. For a concrete method start there, then follow its family route; do not open the entire package.

| Family / public entry | Facade → native binding → engine / canonical rule |
|---|---|
| Open, as-of, versions, checkout | `python/python/lance/__init__.py:137-344` → `python/python/lance/dataset.py:857-945,3263-3297` → `python/src/dataset.rs:930-1070,2274-2279` → `rust/lance/src/dataset.rs:520-588,1459-1474`; as-of selection uses timestamps strictly **before** cutoff when explicit version is absent |
| scanner, to_table, to_batches | `python/python/lance/dataset.py:1496-1565,7348-7409` → `python/src/dataset.rs:1232-1437` → `python/src/scanner.rs:34-49` → `python/src/reader.rs:48-123` → `rust/lance/src/dataset/scanner.rs:2632-2675,3210-3375` |
| take/count | `python/python/lance/dataset.py:2304-2310,2616-2622` → `python/src/dataset.rs:1656-1685` → `rust/lance/src/dataset.rs:1705-1778`; projection transform and name-list choices stay mutually exclusive |
| write_dataset / insert | `python/python/lance/dataset.py:8038-8377` → `python/src/dataset.rs:4849-4888` → `rust/lance/src/dataset.rs:950-979` → `rust/lance/src/dataset/write/insert.rs:98-166,202-315` → [commit protocol](protocol-commit.md) |
| delete/update | `python/python/lance/dataset.py:2938-2943,3147-3158` → `python/src/dataset.rs:2006-2098` → `rust/lance/src/dataset/write/delete.rs` or `rust/lance/src/dataset/write/update.rs` via the [declaration directory](api-reference/lance.md) → [conflict contract](protocol-commit.md) |
| create scalar/vector index | `python/python/lance/dataset.py:3905-3932,4575-4606` → `python/src/dataset.rs:2616-2884` → `rust/lance/src/index/create.rs:161-236,659-735` → selected scalar/vector build set in [index protocol](protocol-index.md) |
| compact_files / distributed Compaction | `python/python/lance/dataset.py:7590-7756` → `python/src/dataset/optimize.rs:479-608` → `rust/lance/src/dataset/optimize.rs:1034-1158,3156-3260,3574-3605` |
| optimize_indices | `python/python/lance/dataset.py:7758-7789` → `python/src/dataset.rs:2587-2613` → `rust/lance/src/index.rs:2577-2729` → scalar/vector branch in `rust/lance/src/index/append.rs:435-613,899-1251` |
| cleanup/explain | `python/python/lance/dataset.py:3366-3499` → `python/src/dataset.rs:2291-2338` → Dataset cleanup API and cleanup/policy entries in [Rust directory](api-reference/lance.md); explain and execute have distinct side effects |
| commit/commit_batch/LanceOperation/Transaction | `python/python/lance/dataset.py:4895-5214,6068-6074,6172-6772` → `python/src/dataset.rs:3091-3260` → CommitBuilder and [frozen operation/codec/application](../L1-modules/rust-lance-table.md) → [commit protocol](protocol-commit.md) |

Other direct-source public families are explicitly reachable through the [Python directory](api-reference/python.md) and [Python Module Map](../L1-modules/python.md): fragment/schema evolution and UDFs; blob descriptors/read/write/sidecars; low-level file Reader/Writer/Session; SQL and DatasetDelta; tags/branches/base paths/storage options; query objects and index configs; statistics/progress/tracing; MemWal sharding/writers/scanners/planners; Torch/TF/Ray integrations and namespace adapters. Their declared interfaces and ownership file are recorded; runtime semantics outside checked contract ranges retain mapped trust. The root export list and native registration lists are separate: imported Session and module-level native classes need not all appear in `__all__`. (python/python/lance/__init__.py:10-134; python/src/lib.rs:255-330)

## Change discipline

Preserve public signatures; deprecate/add rather than silently breaking callers. Keep validation/business logic in Rust and parameter names consistent across Rust/Python/Java. An API extension normally changes the Python declaration/argument forwarding, PyO3 signature/conversion, Rust builder/validation and documentation together. Mutually exclusive modes should use a mode/enum rather than new boolean combinations. (AGENTS.md:52-57; python/AGENTS.md:33-36)

For a new scanner option, the first five files are `python/python/lance/dataset.py:1223-1565,7348-7385`, `python/src/dataset.rs:1232-1437`, `rust/lance/src/dataset/scanner.rs:3210-3375` plus its setter in [Rust declarations](api-reference/lance.md), `rust/lance-datafusion/src/planner.rs:280-350` only for expression semantics, and the selected execution node from the [Dataset map](../L1-modules/rust-lance.md). Changes to Java follow its mapped-only JNI route as a separate subtask. No external Arrow/Pandas/PyO3 implementation is part of this KB.
